newsitem.title: UK: Lauda Air to axe cargo fuel surcharges.
newsitem.headline: Lauda Air to axe cargo fuel surcharges.

text.p: Lauda Air will abolish the cargo fuel surcharges introduced on December 15 with effect from end-April, its UK cargo general sales agent Tony Hardy told Reuters.
Hardy, managing director of London-based Aviacargo said Lauda currently levied ex-UK surcharges of three pence per kg on European flights and six pence on long-haul services.
"These will be lifted, as will all other Lauda cargo fuel surcharges system-wide," he said.
"This is only fair," he added, explaining that jet fuel prices had fallen from a summer 1996 high to a more reasonable level that did not warrant surcharges.
